outputs.L3:
The LED device includes a substrate on which multiple LED units are formed. The LED units may be arranged in an array or in another suitable pattern on the substrate to provide a desired light-emitting area and electrical configuration.

Each LED unit includes a first semiconductor layer and a second semiconductor layer. The first semiconductor layer and the second semiconductor layer are configured to participate in light generation when an electrical current is applied to the LED unit. Each LED unit also includes three sidewalls, including a first sidewall and a second sidewall opposite to the first sidewall.

A first group of conductive connecting structures is formed on the first sidewall of one of the LED units. The conductive connecting structures in the first group are arranged to electrically connect the LED units to one another, thereby allowing current to be transmitted between adjacent or corresponding LED units.

A second group of conductive connecting structures is formed on the second sidewall of the same LED unit. The second sidewall is opposite to the first sidewall. Similar to the first group, the conductive connecting structures in the second group electrically connect the LED units to one another. By providing conductive connecting structures on opposite sidewalls of the LED unit, the LED device can achieve improved electrical interconnection and a more flexible circuit layout.

Each conductive connecting structure includes a middle part and two extending parts connected to the middle part. The two extending parts extend from the middle part and have different lengths. This unequal-length configuration may facilitate connection between LED units positioned at different locations or may accommodate the layout of the LED units on the substrate. As a result, the conductive connecting structures provide reliable electrical connection while allowing the LED units to be efficiently arranged on the substrate.
outputs.L4:
A light-emitting diode (LED) device design is provided in which a plurality of LED units are arranged on a common substrate and electrically interconnected through conductive connecting structures formed along sidewall regions of the LED units. Each LED unit may include a semiconductor light-emitting stack, electrodes, and associated insulating or passivation layers, and the LED units may be disposed in an array or other predetermined layout according to the requirements of the final device.

In this design, the electrical connection between adjacent LED units is achieved by using groups of conductive connecting structures positioned on opposite sidewalls of the LED units. The connecting structures may include metal traces, conductive bridges, plated conductors, or other electrically conductive members extending from one LED unit toward another. Unlike conventional arrangements in which the same number of connectors or symmetrical connector shapes are used on opposing sides, the present configuration employs an asymmetric arrangement. For example, a first sidewall of an LED unit may include a first group of conductive connecting structures, while an opposite second sidewall may include a second group having a different number of conductive connecting structures.

In addition to using unequal numbers of conductive connectors, the connecting structures may also include extending portions of different lengths. A connector on one sidewall may extend farther outward or along the substrate than a connector on the opposite sidewall. These differing extension lengths allow the conductive paths to be routed more freely around neighboring LED units, contact pads, insulating regions, or other device components. As a result, the interconnection pattern can be adapted to a wide variety of LED array layouts without requiring excessive spacing between LED units.

The asymmetric connector arrangement improves flexibility in designing series, parallel, or mixed series-parallel electrical connections among the LED units. Because the number and length of the conductive connecting structures can be selected independently on different sidewalls, the designer can optimize current flow, reduce routing congestion, and make better use of the available substrate area. This is particularly useful in compact LED packages, high-density LED arrays, micro-LED displays, and other applications where efficient layout and reliable electrical interconnection are important.

By enabling unequal connector distribution and varied extending-part lengths, the described LED device structure provides improved layout efficiency while maintaining dependable electrical connection between LED units. The design can reduce unnecessary routing complexity, increase arrangement freedom, and support more compact or higher-density LED device configurations.
outputs.L5:
LED stands for “Light Emitting Diode.” It is a modern lighting technology that produces light when an electric current passes through a semiconductor. LEDs are widely used because they are energy-efficient, long-lasting, and available in many colors and brightness levels.

One of the biggest advantages of LED lighting is its low energy consumption. Compared with traditional incandescent bulbs, LEDs use much less electricity while producing the same amount of light. This helps reduce electricity bills and lowers environmental impact. LEDs also have a much longer lifespan, often lasting tens of thousands of hours before needing replacement.

LEDs are used in many areas of daily life. They can be found in home lighting, streetlights, car headlights, televisions, computer screens, smartphones, signs, and decorative lighting. Because they are small, durable, and flexible, LEDs are suitable for both practical and creative applications.

Another important benefit of LEDs is that they produce less heat than older lighting technologies. This makes them safer and more efficient. Many LED products are also dimmable and can be controlled by smart systems, allowing users to adjust brightness and color depending on their needs.

In conclusion, LED technology has changed the way we use light. It is efficient, reliable, and environmentally friendly, making it one of the most important lighting solutions in the modern world.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an LED device invention in formal patent language, specifying sidewalls, semiconductor layers, and conductive connecting structures having middle and extending parts of different lengths.
counterfactuals.output:
An optoelectronic semiconductor device is disclosed. The device comprises a light-emitting diode structure including a semiconductor stack disposed over a substrate, the semiconductor stack comprising a first conductivity-type semiconductor layer, an active light-emitting layer disposed on the first conductivity-type semiconductor layer, and a second conductivity-type semiconductor layer disposed on the active light-emitting layer. The semiconductor stack includes a plurality of sidewalls defining a mesa region, wherein at least one of the sidewalls extends obliquely or substantially vertically relative to a major surface of the substrate.

A first conductive contact is electrically coupled to the first conductivity-type semiconductor layer, and a second conductive contact is electrically coupled to the second conductivity-type semiconductor layer. An insulating layer is disposed on at least a portion of the semiconductor stack and covers at least part of one or more sidewalls of the semiconductor stack. The insulating layer includes one or more openings exposing corresponding portions of the semiconductor layers for electrical connection.

The device further comprises a conductive connecting structure disposed over the insulating layer and electrically connected to one of the first conductive contact and the second conductive contact through a corresponding opening in the insulating layer. The conductive connecting structure includes a middle part and a plurality of extending parts extending outwardly from the middle part. The extending parts are arranged along different directions over the semiconductor stack or toward peripheral regions of the device. At least two of the extending parts have different lengths measured from the middle part to respective distal ends thereof.

In some embodiments, the middle part of the conductive connecting structure is positioned over a central region of the semiconductor stack, and the extending parts extend toward different sidewalls of the semiconductor stack. A first extending part extends toward a first sidewall and has a first length, and a second extending part extends toward a second sidewall and has a second length different from the first length. The difference in length may be selected according to the shape of the mesa region, current spreading requirements, bonding-pad placement, or avoidance of an isolation trench or sidewall portion.

The conductive connecting structure may comprise a metal layer, a transparent conductive layer, or a multilayer conductive stack. The conductive connecting structure is configured to distribute current laterally across the semiconductor stack, thereby improving current spreading and enhancing light-emission uniformity. The middle part may have a width greater than, equal to, or less than a width of one or more of the extending parts. The distal ends of the extending parts may be spaced apart from the sidewalls by different distances.

In one embodiment, the semiconductor stack has a polygonal top-view profile including a first sidewall, a second sidewall, a third sidewall, and a fourth sidewall. The conductive connecting structure includes the middle part, a first extending part extending from the middle part toward the first sidewall, a second extending part extending from the middle part toward the second sidewall, and a third extending part extending from the middle part toward the third sidewall, wherein the first extending part has a length greater than a length of the second extending part and different from a length of the third extending part. The arrangement provides asymmetric current distribution adapted to the geometry of the semiconductor stack.

The invention also includes a light-emitting diode package comprising the above-described optoelectronic semiconductor device mounted on a carrier and electrically connected to external terminals. The conductive connecting structure having extending parts of different lengths enables reduced current crowding, improved optical output, and enhanced reliability while permitting flexible electrode routing relative to the sidewalls of the semiconductor layers.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
